draft.shortGloss: to have; to hold; to have to
notes: Tener is one of the most common verbs in Spanish. It is irregular in the present tense (tengo, tienes, tiene...).

Do not confuse tener with haber. Tener means to possess or hold something physically or abstractly, while haber is used as an auxiliary verb to form compound tenses (e.g., he comido) or to indicate existence (hay).

senses.definition: To possess, own, or hold something in your hands or in your possession.

examples.text: Tengo un coche nuevo en el estacionamiento.
examples.translation: I have a new car in the parking lot.
examples.emotion: proud and excited about the new purchase

senses.definition: To experience a physical or mental state, such as hunger, thirst, age, or cold.

examples.text: Tengo mucha sed después de correr.
examples.translation: I am very thirsty after running.
examples.emotion: tired and eager for a glass of water

senses.definition: To be obliged or forced to do something.

examples.text: Tengo que estudiar español esta noche.
examples.translation: I have to study Spanish tonight.
examples.emotion: determined and slightly overwhelmed by the workload
